claims.statement: repeat() does not enforce its declared 'count is a nonnegative safe integer' precondition: -1, NaN, 2.5, 0.5 and 3.7 are all silently accepted and none throws.
classify(NaN) returns 'positive', which is inside the declared union yet outside common sense.
Mutating add()'s BODY (a+b to a*b) leaves the emitted .d.ts byte-identical, so the type surface cannot see a semantic-only change; mutating the signature does change it.
repeat() is not atomic: a throwing callback leaves values already delivered with no rollback.
MAX_RETRIES carries the fixture's most rigid type (literal 3) and is referenced nowhere else in the file (1 textual occurrence: its own declaration).
Placement matters: a plain comment channel failed to detect the body mutation, while a generated sidecar did.
All five experiment claims re-derive from execution via verify-run-note.mjs (exit 0).
The run's descriptive verbosity transfers to other source. Nothing here measures real-code recall, cost or safety.
